sources.summary: DC BLOX's Greenville location page describes its Greenville data center at 33 Global Drive, Greenville, South Carolina 29607, in the Global Business Park off I-85: 'The colocation data center, designed to Uptime Institute's Tier III standards, is the first-of-its-kind multi-tenant data center located in South Carolina', the first in the state to receive Uptime Institute's Tier III Certification of Constructed Facility for Data Hall 2, and says in the present tense that 'Customers of this data center have access to DC BLOX's full range of colocation and connectivity'. Building specifications: up to 54,000 sq ft of data hall space; 6,700 sq ft of tenant space; precast concrete shell; security includes perimeter fencing, a vehicle gate, campus-wide CCTV and a 24x7x365 manned security desk; power up to 3 MW critical load in phase 1, expandable up to 18 MW, with N+1 generator and UPS backup. The page header gives '3 Data Centers (Operational & in Development)', 36,493 square feet and 8 critical MW 'Committed & Planned' for the market as a whole. Its structured data publish the coordinate latitude 34.8069902, longitude -82.3448072.

sources.summary: The approved minutes record that, under Scheduled Item 14 'Corrigan Farms Rezone', the City Council on 20 October 2026 adopted item 14.A, 'An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Corrigan Farms', by a unanimous vote after the Senior Planner described the applicant's request to rezone the property to the RTI Overlay Zone, the 6 October 2026 public hearing and the Planning Commission's recommendation of approval; and adopted item 14.B, 'An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Corrigan Farms Development Agreement', by a 4:1 vote after the City Attorney explained that the agreement accompanies the rezone and highlighted the updates the Council had requested. sources.title: Eagle Mountain City Council: agenda packet for the regular meeting of 20 October 2026 (Corrigan Farms rezone and development agreement items)
sources.summary: The agenda (item 14.A background) states that 'Corrigan Farms LLC seeks to rezone parcel number 59:068:0006 to add the RTI overlay zone to the property to allow it to potentially develop a data center project with a natural gas power plant.' The development-agreement staff report (item 14.B) says the agreement 'accompanies the rezone of a 41-acre parcel owned by Corrigan Farms LLC to the RTI Overlay Zone and establishes development and infrastructure requirements for the anticipated data center project', that the parcel 'abuts other data center properties', that the agreement is consistent with other data center development agreements except for a 20-year term, and that 'It is anticipated that the applicant will construct 2 data centers with an on site natural gas power plant.' The attached draft agreement (Draft 10-13) between the City and Corrigan Farms, LLC recites that the Company owns approximately 40.99 acres of undeveloped land and proposes a multi-phase Project with 'the uses of one or more data centers' and related power, cooling and electrical facilities; it vests no power-generation rights and lists the remaining approvals (RTI site plan by the Development Review Committee, plats, grading permit, building permits). The rezone staff report gives 40.99 acres, adjacent to existing RTI on the north, east and south, notes that QTS currently uses the property for temporary operational trailers, and its exhibit map marks the subject property south of 1000 North Street beside the QTS and Meta campuses; the presentation says there is no development proposal at this time.
